import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

MAX_DRIVERS = 2

def design(feats):
    # Calculate effect sizes and p-values for all features
    effects = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        x = feats.x[:, i]
        y = feats.y
        mean_y1 = np.mean(x[y == 1])
        mean_y0 = np.mean(x[y == 0])
        effect_size = mean_y1 - mean_y0
        t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(x[y == 1], x[y == 0], equal_var=False)
        effects.append((fid, effect_size, abs(t_stat), p_val))
    
    # Sort by effect size (absolute value) and p-value
    effects.sort(key=lambda x: (-abs(x[1]), x[3]))
    
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    keep = []
    correlations = {}
    
    # Build correlation matrix
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x.T)
    
    for i, (fid1, _, _, _) in enumerate(effects):
        is_duplicate = False
        for j, fid2 in enumerate(keep):
            if abs(corr_matrix[i, feats.column(fid2)]) >= 0.6:
                is_duplicate = True
                break
        if not is_duplicate:
            keep.append(fid1)
            if len(keep) >= MAX_DRIVERS:
                break
    
    # Select top drivers
    drivers = tuple(keep[:MAX_DRIVERS])
    
    # Use all features with significant associations
    columns = tuple([fid for fid, _, _, p in effects if p < 0.05])
    
    # Check for interaction terms between top features
    products = []
    for i, fid1 in enumerate(columns):
        for j, fid2 in enumerate(columns[i+1:], i+1):
            if abs(corr_matrix[feats.column(fid1), feats.column(fid2)]) >= 0.6:
                products.append((fid1, fid2))
    
    # Weighted score using top features
    loadings = {fid: 1.0 for fid in columns}
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
